# The 9 methods, in one line each {#methods-what}

What each one does, and why it earns a place in the toolbox. Click a method:

```{ojs}
methodInfo = [
  {name:"PCA",
   what:"Takes one data matrix and finds the few directions along which the samples vary the most, then rewrites each sample with coordinates along those directions instead of the original variables.",
   why:"The workhorse for dimension reduction and visualization — and the building block the others extend."},
  {name:"PLSKERN",
   what:"Given predictors X and a response Y on the same samples, it builds components of X that vary together with Y (maximizing their covariance) — supervised, unlike PCA. The 'kernel' part is just a faster route to the same fit via cross-product matrices.",
   why:"Handles many correlated variables (p ≫ n) where ordinary regression fails; the kernel form is a fast route to the same PLS fit."},
  {name:"CCA",
   what:"Takes two data blocks X and Y measured on the same samples and finds the weighted combination of each whose resulting scores are as correlated as possible — i.e. the strongest shared pattern between the two blocks.",
   why:"Quantifies how two sets of measurements on the same samples relate — the classic two-block tool."},
  {name:"PMD",
   what:"Approximates a matrix as a sum of rank-1 pieces (score × loading), but with penalties that push most loading weights to exactly zero — a low-rank factorization that is also sparse.",
   why:"The engine behind sparse PCA/CCA — gives interpretable factors by zeroing out most loadings."},
  {name:"SPC",
   what:"PCA with a sparsity penalty: each principal component is still a direction of high variance, but it's allowed to use only a small subset of variables (the rest get weight zero).",
   why:"Keeps PCA's structure but yields loadings you can actually read — a named short list per component."},
  {name:"SCCA",
   what:"CCA with sparsity: it finds the correlated directions between two blocks X and Z, but forces each direction to rely on only a few variables per block instead of all of them.",
   why:"Finds which specific variables in each block drive the association — feasible even when p ≫ n."},
  {name:"JIVE",
   what:"Takes several data types measured on the same samples and decomposes each into three parts: a joint structure shared across all types, individual structure unique to that type, and residual noise.",
   why:"Separates signal common to all sources from what's unique to each — what plain PCA/CCA can't do."},
   {name:"PLS-DA",
   what:"PLS turned into a classifier: the response is the class label (one-hot encoded), so it finds the directions of X that best separate the known groups. Uses all variables — the dense counterpart of sPLS-DA.",
   why:"Supervised group separation and prediction when variables are many and correlated (p ≫ n)."},
  {name:"sPLS-DA",
   what:"PLS used for classification: the response is the class label (one-hot encoded), and a sparsity penalty makes each component depend on only a few variables — so it separates the classes and names the variables doing it.",
   why:"Predicts the class and names the few variables responsible — interpretable biomarker selection."}
]
```

````{ojs}
viewof methodSel = {
  const wrap=html`<div style="display:flex;gap:7px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:14px"></div>`;
  const els=methodInfo.map((d,k)=>{ const b=html`<button>${d.name}</button>`;
    b.style.cssText="font:700 13px inherit;padding:6px 13px;border-radius:20px;border:1.5px solid #ddd;background:#fff;color:#555;cursor:pointer";
    b.onclick=()=>{wrap.value=k;render();wrap.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("input"));}; return b; });
  els.forEach(e=>wrap.append(e));
  const render=()=>els.forEach((b,k)=>{ const on=k===wrap.value;
    b.style.background=on?"#E78824":"#fff"; b.style.borderColor=on?"#E78824":"#ddd"; b.style.color=on?"#fff":"#555"; });
  wrap.value=0; render(); return wrap;
}
````

````{ojs}
methodView = {
  const d=methodInfo[methodSel];
  const O="#E78824",Od="#C14C23",G="#4D701F",ink="#2a2a2a",mut="#777";
  const card=html`<div style="border:2px solid #eee;border-top:5px solid ${O};border-radius:14px;padding:18px 24px;background:#fff;min-height:180px"></div>`;
  card.append(html`<div style="font:800 24px inherit;color:${Od};margin-bottom:14px">${d.name}</div>`);
  const block=(label,text,col)=>{
    const b=html`<div style="margin-bottom:14px"></div>`;
    b.append(html`<div style="font:800 12px inherit;letter-spacing:.04em;color:${col};margin-bottom:3px">${label}</div>`);
    b.append(html`<div style="font:400 17px inherit;line-height:1.45;color:${ink}">${text}</div>`);
    return b;
  };
  card.append(block("WHAT IT IS", d.what, G));
  card.append(block("WHY IT MATTERS", d.why, O));
  return card;
}
````



# How the 9 methods differ {#methods-diff}

Read a cell as **row vs column**: what the row method has/does that the column one doesn't.

```{ojs}
methodsDiff = {
  const names = ["PCA","PLSKERN","CCA","PMD","SPC","SCCA","JIVE","PLS-DA","sPLS-DA"];
  // D[i][j] = how row i differs from column j (short phrase)
  const D = {
    "PCA":      {"PLSKERN":"no Y — unsuper vised", "CCA":"one block, variance not correlation", "PMD":"dense, no sparsity", "SPC":"dense loadings", "SCCA":"one block, dense", "JIVE":"single data type", "PLS-DA":"unsuper vised, no labels", "sPLS-DA":"no labels"},
    "PLSKERN":  {"PCA":"uses Y (supervised)", "CCA":"max covariance, not correlation", "PMD":"dense, regression-oriented", "SPC":"supervised, dense", "SCCA":"two-block but dense", "JIVE":"one X–Y pair, no joint/indiv", "PLS-DA":"regression Y, not classes", "sPLS-DA":"regression Y, not classes/sparse"},
    "CCA":      {"PCA":"two blocks, correlation", "PLSKERN":"correlation, not covariance", "PMD":"dense, symmetric X–Y", "SPC":"two-block, dense", "SCCA":"dense (no selection)", "JIVE":"shared only, no individual", "PLS-DA":"unsuper vised, not classification", "sPLS-DA":"unsupervised, dense"},
    "PMD":      {"PCA":"adds sparsity penalty", "PLSKERN":"matrix factori zation, not regression", "CCA":"penalized, sparse factors", "SPC":"general engine (SPC is a use of it)", "SCCA":"general engine (SCCA uses it)", "JIVE":"single matrix", "PLS-DA":"unsuper vised, no classes", "sPLS-DA":"unsupervised, no classes"},
    "SPC":      {"PCA":"sparse loadings", "PLSKERN":"unsupervised + sparse", "CCA":"one block + sparse", "PMD":"specific case (sparse PCA)", "SCCA":"one block, not two", "JIVE":"single type, sparse", "PLS-DA":"unsuper vised, no labels", "sPLS-DA":"no labels"},
    "SCCA":     {"PCA":"two blocks + sparse", "PLSKERN":"correlation + sparse", "CCA":"adds variable selection", "PMD":"specific case (sparse CCA)", "SPC":"two blocks, not one", "JIVE":"shared only, sparse", "PLS-DA":"unsupervised two-block", "sPLS-DA":"unsupervised X–Z"},
    "JIVE":     {"PCA":"≥2 types, splits joint/indiv", "PLSKERN":"≥2 types, no response", "CCA":"adds individual structure", "PMD":"multi-type decom position", "SPC":"multi-type, not sparse", "SCCA":"joint + individual (not just shared)", "PLS-DA":"unsuper vised integration", "sPLS-DA":"unsupervised integration"},
    "PLS-DA":   {"PCA":"supervised — uses class labels", "PLSKERN":"classifies (class Y), not regression", "CCA":"supervised classi fication", "PMD":"supervised, uses classes", "SPC":"supervised, uses classes", "SCCA":"classify, not correlate", "JIVE":"classification, single X", "sPLS-DA":"dense — uses all variables"},
    "sPLS-DA":  {"PCA":"supervised classi fication", "PLSKERN":"class labels + sparse", "CCA":"classify, not correlate", "PMD":"supervised, classes", "SPC":"supervised + selection", "SCCA":"Y = class indicator", "JIVE":"classi fication, one X", "PLS-DA":"adds sparsity (variable selection)"}
  };
  const O="#E78824",Od="#C14C23",G="#4D701F",ink="#2a2a2a",mut="#555";
  const box=html`<div style="overflow:auto;max-height:560px"></div>`;
  const tbl=html`<table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:inherit;font-size:10px;table-layout:fixed;width:100%"></table>`;
  const hr=html`<tr></tr>`;
  hr.append(html`<th style="position:sticky;left:0;top:0;z-index:3;background:#fff;width:62px"></th>`);
  names.forEach(n=>{
    const th=html`<th>${n}</th>`;
    th.style.cssText=`position:sticky;top:0;z-index:2;background:#fff;padding:4px 3px;font-size:10.5px;font-weight:800;color:${Od};border-bottom:2px solid ${O}`;
    hr.append(th);
  });
  tbl.append(hr);
  names.forEach((ri)=>{
    const tr=html`<tr></tr>`;
    const rh=html`<th>${ri}</th>`;
    rh.style.cssText=`position:sticky;left:0;background:#fff;z-index:1;padding:4px 5px;text-align:right;font-size:10.5px;font-weight:800;color:${Od};border-right:2px solid ${O}`;
    tr.append(rh);
    names.forEach((ci)=>{
      if(ri===ci){
        const td=html`<td>${ri}</td>`;
        td.style.cssText=`background:#fff2e6;color:${G};font-weight:800;text-align:center;padding:4px;border:1px solid #f0e6d8;font-size:10px`;
        tr.append(td);
      } else {
        const td=html`<td>${D[ri][ci]}</td>`;
        td.style.cssText=`padding:4px 5px;border:1px solid #eee;color:${ink};line-height:1.25;vertical-align:top`;
        tr.append(td);
      }
    });
    tbl.append(tr);
  });
  box.append(tbl);
  return box;
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof benchPick = {
  const names = Object.keys(benchAll);
  const wrap=html`<div style="display:flex;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:12px"></div>`;
  const els=names.map((nm)=>{ const b=html`<button>${nm}</button>`;
    b.style.cssText="font:700 12.5px inherit;padding:5px 12px;border-radius:20px;border:1.5px solid #ddd;background:#fff;color:#555;cursor:pointer";
    b.onclick=()=>{wrap.value=nm;render();wrap.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("input"));}; return b; });
  els.forEach(e=>wrap.append(e));
  const render=()=>els.forEach((b,k)=>{ const on=names[k]===wrap.value;
    b.style.background=on?"#E78824":"#fff"; b.style.borderColor=on?"#E78824":"#ddd"; b.style.color=on?"#fff":"#555"; });
  wrap.value=names[0]; render(); return wrap;
}
```

```{ojs}
benchTable = {
  const d=benchAll[benchPick];
  const O="#E78824",Od="#C14C23",G="#4D701F",ink="#2a2a2a",mut="#777";
  const box=html`<div></div>`;
  box.append(html`<div style="font:700 13px inherit;color:${mut};margin-bottom:8px">${benchPick} &nbsp;·&nbsp; reference: <span style="color:${ink}">${d.ref}</span> &nbsp;·&nbsp; <span style="color:${G};font-weight:800">all sizes IDENTICAL ✓</span></div>`);

  const head = d.rjulia
    ? ["Size","Match","Julia time","J alloc","J mem","Ref time","Ref alloc","Ref mem"]
    : ["Size","Match","Julia time","J alloc","J mem","Ref time (R)","R reps"];

  const tbl=html`<table style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:12.5px;font-family:inherit"></table>`;
  const hr=html`<tr></tr>`;
  head.forEach((h,i)=>{ const th=html`<th>${h}</th>`;
    th.style.cssText=`text-align:${i===0?'left':'center'};padding:5px 7px;border-bottom:2px solid ${O};color:${ink};font-weight:800;font-size:11.5px`;
    hr.append(th); });
  tbl.append(hr);

  d.rows.forEach((r,ri)=>{
    const cells = d.rjulia
      ? [r[0],r[1],r[2],r[3],r[4],r[5],r[6],r[7]]   // size,match,jt,ja,jm,rt,ra,rm
      : [r[0],r[1],r[2],r[3],r[4],r[5],r[8]];        // size,match,jt,ja,jm,rt,reps
    const refTimeIdx = 5;
    const tr=html`<tr></tr>`; tr.style.background= ri%2 ? "#faf8f5":"#fff";
    cells.forEach((c,ci)=>{
      const td=html`<td>${c}</td>`;
      let css=`padding:4px 7px;text-align:${ci===0?'left':'center'};border-bottom:1px solid #eee;`;
      if(ci===0) css+=`font-weight:700;color:${ink};`;
      else if(ci===1) css+=`font-family:ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;font-size:11px;color:${G};`;
      else if(ci===2) css+=`font-weight:800;color:${G};`;
      else if(ci===refTimeIdx) css+=`color:${Od};font-weight:700;`;
      else css+=`color:${mut};font-size:11.5px;`;
      td.style.cssText=css;
      tr.append(td);
    });
    tbl.append(tr);
  });
  box.append(tbl);
  return box;
}
```

<div class="uthsc-green-box" style="font-size:0.72em; padding:6px 12px;">
All 8 methods reproduce their reference at every size (worst 1.1e-13; sparse methods also match <b>selected sets</b>). For Julia references (PCA, PLSKERN, CCA) the reference's allocations and memory are shown too; R references report time only. JIVE compared by joint-subspace canonical corr (shown as 1−corr). Julia = <code>@btime</code> best-case; R = <code>microbenchmark</code> median (<b>20 reps small / 3 large</b>), in-R, excludes RCall overhead — separate runtimes, not a direct ratio. SCCA 3000×4000+5000: R skipped (27M cells).
</div>
